THE WRONG LESSON

The model is not the interface.

The best interface is no interface. The model gets good enough, you type what you want, it does it. That is the argument, and it is a good one.

It is also the plot of 2001. The computer runs the entire ship. There are no stations, no screens, no controls — just a calm voice that is always certain. It works beautifully right up until you need to disagree with it, and by then the only interface left is a screwdriver and a crawlspace.

The other option is a bridge. Everybody has a station, a screen and an opinion. The captain can see what any of them sees. Somebody tells you the engines will not take it, and he is usually right.

I love Computer. Sometimes I want to talk to Scotty.

01

It reads the terminal, and prefers what each agent says about itself in a few agreed lines.

02

The one that needs you gets a question mark over its head. Leave it and the mark gets louder.

03

A LIVING OPERATING PICTURE

See the whole kitchen.

Not another board full of stale cards. Your agents are already working; Pizza Fleet draws them, so that knowing which one is stuck costs you a glance instead of a search.

  • Every agent becomes a character with a face.
  • The one waiting on you gets a question mark over its head.
  • Its screen appears above it when you click.
  • Ignore it long enough and it stops saying “a question awaits” and starts saying “the party is blocked”.
